chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man were to marry a girl who was a breast-fed infant, and his wife breast-fed her, then his marriage is void.

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man's wife who breast-fed a girl; would she be permissible for his son from another woman?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'So she is placed in the status of a sister through breast-feeding?' He said: 'Yes, from the side of the father.'

key_terms.رَضِيعاً: an infant who has been breast-fed
key_terms.مِنْ قِبَلِ الْأَبِ: from the side of the father (indicating the specific kinship link)

ai.seo_question: How does a wife's breast-feeding affect the marriageability of her husband to the breast-fed girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific mechanism of 'radh'' (breast-feeding) establishing kinship, particularly highlighting the unique Shia scholarly view that the husband's connection to the wet nurse is direct ('from the side of the father'), thereby creating a barrier to marriage for him. It clarifies that if a man's wife breast-feeds a girl, she becomes his daughter-in-law (or sister-in-law in the sense of being the wife of his son), rendering her unlawful to him if already married, yet permissible for his other sons. This ruling underscores the depth of kinship ties formed through nursing, extending beyond biological lineage to create permanent marital prohibitions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If a man were to marry a girl having been breast-fed by his wife, so his marriage is void’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a wife of a man who breast-feeds a girl, would she be correct for her children from someone else?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘So she would have come down to be at the status of the sister from the breast-feeding?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, from the direction of the father’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a man marries a small girl and she is breastfed by his wife his marriage becomes invalid.’

I then asked about the case of woman of a man who breastfeeds a girl; if her sons from another husband can marry her (the girl). He (the Imam) said, ‘No, they cannot do so.’ I then asked, ‘Is she like a sister of breastfeeding?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, from the side of the father.’”
